questions.question: What is the maximum of a set $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$?
options: Any upper bound of $E$
Any lower bound of $E$
The smallest element outside $E$
The largest element of $E$, if it exists

questions.question: If $\max E = x$, which condition must hold?
options: $x\notin E$ and $x\ \ge y$ for all $y\in E$
$x\in E$ and $x\ \le y$ for all $y\in E$
$x\in E$ and $x\ \ge y$ for all $y\in E$
$x$ is any real number

questions.question: What is the maximum of $\{1,2,3\}$?
options: The set has no maximum

questions.question: Which listed set has no maximum?
What is true about maxima?
options: A set can have many different maxima
Every bounded set has a maximum
A set can have at most one maximum
A maximum never belongs to the set

questions.question: How is the maximum related to the least upper bound when it exists?
options: The maximum is never an upper bound
The maximum is always smaller than the least upper bound
The maximum is a lower bound only
The maximum is the least upper bound for the set

questions.question: For $E = \{2,5,7\}$, which value satisfies the definition of $\max E$?
For $E = (0,1]$, what is $\max E$?
options: No maximum
$\frac12$

questions.question: Why does the interval $(0,1)$ have upper bounds but no maximum?
options: Because no number is greater than elements of $(0,1)$
Because every element of $(0,1)$ is equal
Because a maximum need not belong to the set
Because $1$ is not an element of $(0,1)$

questions.question: Which statement distinguishes a maximum from a general upper bound?
options: An upper bound must always be an element of the set
A maximum must be an element of the set
A maximum need not be at least all elements
An upper bound is always smaller than every element

questions.question: A student claims that $1$ is the maximum of $(0,1)$. What is the error?
options: $1\notin(0,1)$, so it cannot be the maximum
$1$ is smaller than every element of $(0,1)$
$(0,1)$ contains no positive numbers
The maximum of any interval must be $0$

questions.question: Suppose $x\in E$ and $x\ \ge y$ for all $y\in E$. What can be concluded?
options: $x$ is only a lower bound
$x = \max E$
$E$ has no maximum
$x$ cannot be an upper bound

questions.question: Does every non-empty finite set of real numbers have a maximum?
options: Yes; finite sets attain a maximum
No; finite sets have no maximum
Only if all elements are positive
Only if it is an interval

questions.question: When $\max E$ exists, how does it relate to $\sup E$?
options: $\max E=\sup E$
$\max E<\sup E$
$\max E>\sup E$
they are unrelated

questions.question: Does the empty set have a maximum?
options: No; no element can be largest
Yes; zero is its largest element
Yes; $+\infty$ is its largest element
Yes; $\varnothing$ is its largest element

questions.question: For finite sets $A,B$, what is $\max(A\cup B)$?
options: $\max(\max A,\max B)$
$\max A+\max B$
$\min(\max A,\max B)$
$\max A\cdot\max B$

questions.question: Which set has maximum $1$?
Which number is an upper bound of $(0,1)$ but not a maximum?
Why does $(0,1)$ have no maximum?
options: It has no upper bounds.
It contains the point $1$.
No element of $(0,1)$ is largest.
It contains only one point.

questions.question: For $E=[-2,3)$, which statement is correct?
options: $E$ has no maximum.
$\max E=3$.
$\max E=-2$, confusing the minimum with the maximum.
$\max E=0$.
